Subject: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to chat earlier — thanks for the time and for walking through the recommendation flow and throughput expectations. Quick recap + our recommended shortlist based on the demo and the benchmarks we ran against your sample dataset:

Key constraints you mentioned:
- 99th pct latency target: <= 350ms for interactive classification paths
- Batch scoring throughput (nightly): ~120k messages / hour
- SRE constraint: prefer a model + config we can run on dedicated capacity with automatic fallback to hosted if we need burst.

Recommended shortlist (rationale in-line):
1) redwood-alpha-7b (quantized int4) — Best balance of cost and latency for high-throughput scoring. Latency 95-200ms on p4d-like instance, token cost low. Quality: strong on classification and reranking; occasional failure mode on very long context.
2) open-vista-13b-8k (float16) — Higher quality for edge-case prompts (longer context), better semantic understanding, but ~2x cost and higher 95th pct latency (~380ms) in our tests. Good candidate for canary and fallback for complex channels.
3) instruct-lite-3b (int8) — Lowest cost, lowest latency (~120ms), acceptable for short classification prompts and for safe default routing. Not recommended for complex multi-turn generation.

Next steps we propose:
- I uploaded the full benchmark CSVs and the prompt set we used: acme_model_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt (Drive link below).
- If you’re ok, we’ll provision a 2-week dedicated trial of redwood-alpha-7b tuned with your caching policy and a small canary using open-vista-13b for the 10% of traffic that needs higher fidelity.
- Pricing estimate attached (redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf).

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the peak concurrent qps we should tune for for interactive API (you mentioned ~180 qps)?
- Any strict PII/data residency constraints beyond the US region?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up tomorrow to lock the MA plan.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
